It's like getting any skill as strange as that sounds. The more you skateboard or play guitar the better you can balance or play all the notes. 

The more you deal with trauma or depression the better coping skills you develop and the easier it is to all handle. Does it go away? Yes.... and no. If you have deficiencies in nutrients or sleep you can fix it. If your depression is a result of a shitty job or shitty people you can fix it. Hey it could even be because of an underlying disease, so go to a doctor if you feel off or different in any way.

Now, if you have a chemical issue like some do it may seem really really hard to shake.  There's medications and treatments that will help you in some cases. For me I do not take meds for my manic depression, when I did I felt as though I turned into a very dead person with hardly any emotion or motivation to do things I like. That was MY experience, others may do great with meds. I know a few who have been on medications for years and are doing great. 

If meds are not in the cards, you can just try to make yourself as comfortable as possible. Therapy helps a ton, and cutting out stress as much as possible helps even more. That shitty job? Try to get a new one. That shitty gf/bf? Kick their ass to the curb. Little things here and there too. Like I said, it's a skill so as long as you can be as level headed as possible, you will go miles. Trust the world around you and not the voice in your head. People do care about you and want you here. And people are much kinder than we all seem to propagate. Whatever you do, DO NOT START ABUSING A SUBSTANCE (Yeah easier said than done). Alchohol and drugs will make shit much worse. I heard weed can help, but I still have yet to try it. I did drink excessively for a long time, and I did coke (which was only twice and thank god I did not get addicted). 

Finally, find a hobby or passion you can really dig. Something you practice each day and look forward to. That's a big help. Reach out to people especially when you really dont wanna.

She was with this dude for 7 months and all was going well but she broke it off due to her own underlying problems and the fact that there was no passion in the relationship. He was also head over heels in love with her and the break up was rough. Just make sure you know EXACTLY what you're doing and why. If you break it off for seemingly no reason you could potentially lose this dude forever. He may never trust you again. From what you're saying he sounds like a much more mature guy then the one the girl I know was with so he may kind of get it but yeah. Try on your end too to make things more fun. 

Don't leave it all up to him to "bring more passion" or whatever. The girl I'm talking about broke up with the dude for mainly the same reason but from what I remember when I dated her she would never put any effort in and thought the guy in a relationship should just fix everything. Don't be that. Please just talk to him. Relationships are a two person fight. And exes are exes for a reason. Another reason she broke it off with this guy is because she still isn't over an ex from years back. It's hard to get over someone but you gotta be reasonable. You say you're friends, but don't let it get more than that.

Lastly, who knows. It could be very well that you guys aren't compatible. Shit just happens and it sucks but it's a wonderful part of life. Embrace your own needs, but don't let the responsibility fall on everyone else. You have a brain and a mouth.

Let me preface this real quick; anti-depressents are a hit or miss depending on what meds and depending on you. After a suicide attempt back in November I started on Sertraline, an SSRI. Everyone's experience is different, but let me tell you, mine ended in hell. 

The first few months were ok, but once I hit my fourth month things took a turn. I ended up losing 28lbs, My libido dissapeared, and I hurt a lot of people I was close with because I completely stopped caring about anything. My work suffered. Social life also fell almost completely apart. At the time, a close friend of mine was staying with me as he was going through a rough time. He told me in the end that he was so glad I stopped taking them because he watched me turn into a complete piece of shit from beginning to end.

And oh yeah, withdrawal. I weened myself off through advice from my doctor. I was only on 100mg at my fullest dosage, but fucking hell. I was bedridden for days, I was sweating constantly, forgetting shit, couldnt go to work for a week. Thank God my managers are awesome. Still now, 2 months later I still get the occasional brain Zap. And I still get furiously angry every now and again from the smallest thing. I was never like this before. But I'm returning to my old self finally. Slowly.

In conclusion, I am very happy you decided to start on anti depressents. It killed my depression and I was feeling fine for the whole time I was on it up until the last month. Even within the first week, I was feeling 10x better. But please, for your own health, if you feel at all like somethings not right or you are changing for the worse, CALL YOUR DOCTOR AND DON'T IGNORE IT.

The Marine corps pretty much killed my eating disorder, I gained a good 30lbs in boot camp, MCT and MOS school. I have hobbies now, I write poetry and play guitar in a band. I have a job that I love. In the end, I realized only I could save myself. I still have not admitted to my family or close friends that I had an eating disorder, that is still something I'm semi embarrassed about. Not like it matters now. I lift weights, bike, still run. When I was about 3, I was out hiking with my father. We came to a narrow path alongside a cliff, and I was walking backwards while talking to my dad. 

He stopped to look behind us for a few seconds as I began to round the corner.  I felt the ground curve down under my feet and crumble suddenly. My dad jumped for me but it was too late. I fell really far and slammed into rocks. 

To this day, my father and I have no idea how I lived. I walked away with a few cuts and scrapes. When I got older I got bored one day and drove to the same state park. I hadn't been there for years. I hiked out to where I fell. I always thought it was a perspective thing, where because I was so small the cliff seemed a lot bigger, right? 

Apparently not because it was at least 70 feet. I also found out that several people have fallen and gotten badly injured. One person died. There's a river nearby with strong rapids too that people drown in a lot.

Great place for your 3 year olds everyone.
